newsitem.title: UK: Irish air cargo surcharged to balance fall in punt.
newsitem.headline: Irish air cargo surcharged to balance fall in punt.

text.p: Airlines lifting cargo from Ireland have been charging a ten percent surcharge during May to compensate for the slide in the value of the Irish punt against sterling.
From June one the surcharge will drop to five percent for most airlines, said Dave O'Riordan operations manager for GSA International based at Shannon airport.
Irish state carrier Aer Lingus has not had to impose a surcharge as its costs and income are both in punts, he added.

Until the slide in the punt against sterling air cargo contracts from Ireland were based on the assumption of near parity between the two currencies. The surcharges have been targetted at eliminating distortions to companies operating in the two currencies for the first six months of this year.

When cargo contracts are renewed for the second half of the year O'Riordan said it is likely rates will be adjusted to take account of currency movements thus making surcharges unnecessary. --Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+5017 --www.racs.com
